title: Dominic and the Orchard
premise: Cyrus Delacroix, a wedding planner who abandoned belief in love after a devastating betrayal, is coerced into his small town's anonymous pen-pal program meant to bridge old feuds between the orchard families and the vineyard owners. His assigned correspondent turns out to be Theo Marchand, the vineyard's stubborn heir and Cyrus's bitterest professional rival, though neither knows it at first, falling for each other through letters under assumed names. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches and Cyrus's biggest wedding collides with Theo's make-or-break season, their identities are exposed at the worst possible moment, shattering both the letters and their fragile trust. Cyrus must choose between the invisible, armored life he built and the risk of letting Theo stay after the last train leaves—ending with Cyrus planning, for the first time in years, a wedding he believes in: their own.
about_author: Oscar Iversen is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade in the hospitality trade before turning to fiction, drawing on the weddings, harvests, and heartbreaks he witnessed along the way. He writes from a converted barn surrounded by too many fruit trees, insisting that every love story deserves a second pressing.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus orchestrates a flawless wedding he feels nothing at, then returns to his empty apartment above the florist's, where a town council letter announces a mandatory pen-pal program between the orchard and vineyard families. He drafts a refusal, then burns it. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Terms of the Truce
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Marchand, drowning in debt and his late father's failing vineyard, is strong-armed by his grandmother into the same pen-pal program as a condition of a crucial loan. He recognizes Cyrus Delacroix's name on the rival list and smirks, imagining the torture of writing to him. Beat: pride as a shield.

chapters.title: Anonymous Correspondence, Rule One
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The program's organizer, Marisol, assigns pseudonyms and forbids revealing identities. Cyrus writes a deliberately cold first letter; the reply that comes back is sharp, funny, and unexpectedly disarming. He tells himself he's only participating to avoid fines. Beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tends the vines alone, mourning his father and resenting the town that wrote the vineyard off. His pen pal's second letter accuses him of arrogance he hasn't even displayed yet, and Theo laughs for the first time in months. Beat: grief cracked open by irritation.

chapters.title: A Wedding in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus scouts an orchard venue for a high-profile society wedding and runs into Theo, who blocks the access road with a tractor and a smile. Their public feud escalates into a shouting match witnessed by half the town. Beat: enemies sharpened by proximity.

chapters.title: Letters Written in Ink and Vinegar
chapters.summary: Alternating letters, dual POV. The pen pals, each convinced they're writing to a friendly stranger, describe their day—including, with delicious irony, their hatred of a certain rival. Both realize they look forward to the mail. Beat: dramatic irony turning sweet.

chapters.title: The Florist's Boy
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus's young assistant, Dev, who Cyrus informally took in years ago, asks why Cyrus never lets anyone past the front door. A flashback reveals the fiancé who stole Cyrus's business and left him bankrupt. Beat: the wound explained, not yet healed.

chapters.title: Rain on the Trellis
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A storm threatens the young vines; Cyrus, driving home from a venue visit, stops and helps without a word, hands in the mud beside his enemy. Neither mentions it in their letters, but both write warmer ones that night. Beat: tenderness smuggled past defenses.

chapters.title: Rule Two: No Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Marisol warns that two participants have deduced each other's identities and been disqualified. Cyrus, half-hoping his pen pal is anyone but Theo, begins cataloguing clues and deliberately stops looking. Beat: denial as self-protection.

chapters.title: The Tasting Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The society wedding's planner requests a wine tasting for the couple—at Theo's vineyard, catered by Cyrus's team. Forced to collaborate for a week, Theo and Cyrus bicker, then linger, then share a bottle after hours that ends almost in a kiss. Beat: the almost.

chapters.title: What I Would Tell You
chapters.summary: Dual POV, letters. Both pen pals confess, in careful anonymity, that they've met someone real they can't have. Each advises the other to be brave—advice neither can take. Beat: longing doubled by irony.

chapters.title: Dev Knows
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Dev, sorting the mail, recognizes the vineyard's distinctive stationery and confronts Cyrus: 'You know who it is, don't you?' Cyrus denies it, but Dev's knowing silence forces him to admit the truth to himself. Beat: the mask slipping.

chapters.title: First Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The loan officer moves the deadline: the vineyard must show harvest revenue by season's end or be sold. Theo, exhausted, writes his pen pal the most honest letter yet—about fear, legacy, and wanting one person who stays. Beat: vulnerability as courage.

chapters.title: The Society Wedding
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The orchard wedding arrives, and Cyrus, running it flawlessly, watches the couple's joy with something like grief. Theo attends as the wine vendor and catches Cyrus crying in the coat room; instead of gloating, he sits with him. Beat: compassion where contempt used to live.

chapters.title: Almost Told
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the coat room's heels, Theo drafts a letter confessing his identity, then burns it when Cyrus publicly snubs him at the harvest festival to protect his professional reputation. Beat: the cost of Cyrus's armor, seen from outside.

chapters.title: The Unsealed Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Marisol, ending the program early, delivers final letters unsealed. Cyrus reads his—and every clue assembles at once: the tractor, the trellis mud, the coat room. His pen pal is Theo. He arrives at the vineyard as Theo realizes the same, and the confrontation is brutal. Beat: identity revealed, trust shattered.

chapters.title: Harvest Without Him
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo throws himself into the harvest, furious and heartbroken, while the loan officer circles. Dev appears with a message Cyrus won't deliver himself: an apology, and the truth about the betrayal that made him. Beat: anger softening into understanding.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus dismantles his armor piece by piece—apologizing publicly at the farmers' market, closing the distance his ex-fiancé taught him to keep. He writes one last letter and leaves it, signed with his real name, in the vineyard's gate. Beat: choosing visibility over safety.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The vineyard's foreclosure auction convenes as the first harvest comes in. Cyrus arrives with the society couple and the town's rallied families; the wedding contract, redirected to the vineyard, saves it. Theo realizes Cyrus planned it like a wedding—every detail, for him. Beat: love as logistics and sacrifice.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The last train of the season leaves at nine. Cyrus waits at the platform past nine-oh-five, certain he's been abandoned, then turns to find Theo running down the road, harvest-stained, having chosen to stay. First kiss, finally unguarded. Beat: staying as the ultimate vow.

chapters.title: A Wedding He Believes In
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Spring: Cyrus plans a wedding in the orchard between the vineyard rows—small, imperfect, real—with Dev as best man and Marisol officiating. He reads his first letter to Theo aloud as his vows. Beat: the cynic converted by his own craft.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Cyrus's POV. Years later, Cyrus and Theo's adopted daughter Dominic presses cider from the orchard's first joint harvest, asking how her fathers met. 'By letter,' Theo says. 'By accident,' Cyrus says. 'On purpose,' they say together. Beat: found family, full circle, the harvest kept.
